title: Financial Counseling Schedule: Screening Ceiling on a Paused Patient Payment Plan
content:
The longest paused schedule of a **Patient Payment Plan** may run past the tier's maximum term only as far as the screening ceiling of the paused schedule allows. The screening is the household federal poverty level (FPL) percentage recorded on the patient's open application in the Financial Assistance Program (Charity Care). A financial assistance application of the patient is open when one of the patient's financial assistance cases in the Financial Assistance Program (Charity Care) stands in submitted or pending documents status, a submitted case being taken first.

**Rule.** The screening ceiling is 60 installments when the open application's household was screened at or below 200 percent of the federal poverty level, and 48 installments when it was screened above 200 and at or below 400 percent, each only on tiers whose maximum term is shorter; otherwise the screening ceiling is the tier's maximum term.

| Tier | Tier maximum term | Screened at or below 200% FPL | Above 200% and at or below 400% FPL | Above 400% FPL, not screened, or no open application |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Riverbend Short-Term Payment Plan | 6 | 60 | 48 | 6 |
| Riverbend Standard Payment Plan | 12 | 60 | 48 | 12 |
| Riverbend Extended Payment Plan | 24 | 60 | 48 | 24 |
| Riverbend Long-Term Payment Plan | 36 | 60 | 48 | 36 |
| Riverbend Assistance-Linked Payment Plan | 48 | 60 | 48 | 48 |
| Riverbend Hardship Payment Plan | 60 | 60 | 60 | 60 |

**Boundaries.** A household screened at exactly 200 percent takes the 60-installment ceiling; at 200.1 percent it takes 48. At exactly 400 percent the ceiling is 48; above 400 percent it is the tier's maximum term.
